NovaBiotech - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaBiotech Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaBiotech's financial results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Raj Singh, Chief Scientific Officer; Karen Lee, Head of Commercial; and Tom Harris, Head of Manufacturing.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO of NovaBiotech.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. NovaBiotech delivered a strong performance in the Q3, driven by robust demand for our flagship products like NOV-GLP1, our once-weekly GLP-1/GIP dual agonist for type 2 diabetes and obesity, ONCO-456, our next-generation antibody-drug conjugate for HER2-positive solid tumors, and RARE-ZEN, our AAV-based gene therapy for Pompe disease. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives, focusing on our pricing and reimbursement landscape, which remains dynamic amid payer pressures; our key assumptions and risk factors shaping guidance; revenue guidance and upcoming catalysts; business development through licensing, acquisitions, and partnerships; geographic revenue breakdown with emerging market momentum; recent regulatory approvals and label expansions; and our R&D expenses alongside pipeline investment priorities.

We are particularly excited about ONCO-456 and its potential to expand into broader HER2-low indications, unlocking billions in peak sales.

Now, I will turn the call over to Mike Chen, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Mike Chen, CFO:
Thank you, Dr. Rivera. As Dr. Rivera mentioned, we had a solid Q3. Revenue for the quarter was $1.62 billion, an increase of 15% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by volume growth in NOV-GLP1 and ONCO-456, alongside initial contributions from RARE-ZEN in new markets.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $380 million, or $2.30 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $450 million, or $2.70 per share.

Our operating expenses were $850 million, reflecting continued investment in R&D to advance our pipeline while achieving efficiencies in SG&A. We continue to invest heavily in innovation, with our cash position remaining strong at $3.2 billion.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to $6.5 to $6.8 billion in revenue, representing 20-25% growth, with key drivers including pipeline catalysts and emerging market expansion.

I'll now turn to our pricing and reimbursement landscape, which remains a dynamic and critical area for NovaBiotech as we navigate evolving payer dynamics across our portfolio. Our flagship products—NOV-GLP1, ONCO-456, and RARE-ZEN—continue to drive the majority of our revenue, representing 78% of Q3 ex-US sales and 65% in the US. But pricing pressures and reimbursement pathways are intensifying, particularly under the Inflation Reduction Act and global health technology assessment reforms. Let me break this down regionally.

In the US, our overall gross-to-net adjustment rate for the quarter stood at 48%, up 320 basis points year-over-year, driven by higher 340B discounts now at 22% of volume and increased PBM rebates on NOV-GLP1 reaching 35-40% in commercial channels, aligning with peers. WAC for NOV-GLP1 is $1,250 per monthly dose, but net prices declined 6.2% YoY to about $675 per dose due to contracting with CVS Caremark, Express Scripts, and OptumRx for preferred formulary access amid GLP-1 demand.

ONCO-456 saw a 4.1% quarter-over-quarter ASP decline to $18,200 per cycle from Medicare rebasing, offset by value-based agreements with five major payers covering 15% of lives, tied to progression-free survival, achieving 92% rebate avoidance via real-world evidence from our ONCO-REALITY registry with over 2,500 patients. RARE-ZEN's orphan status keeps net pricing at $2.8 million per course, though 340B erodes 12%.

Ahead, IRA negotiations risk 25-30% cuts post-2026, but biologics are shielded; we've reallocated $150 million in R&D to bispecifics.

In Europe, we've secured HTA nods for NOV-GLP1 in 12 of 15 markets, like NICE at 22% discount for €850 net per dose. ONCO-456 got IQWiG's "considerable added benefit" in Germany for full AMNOG at €15,400 per cycle, despite biosimilar pressures projecting 8-10% volume shifts.

Ex-US shines: Japan NHI list drove 45% NOV-GLP1 growth at ¥180,000 per dose; China NRDL for RARE-ZEN at 62% discount unlocks $250 million peak by 2027, echoing Gilead's HCV success.

Industry-wide, US net pricing erodes 5-7% annually per SSR Health, with GLP-1s at 55% new scripts but 40% coverage. Globally, 28% of our contracts are outcomes-linked, up from 12%, via Global Evidence Network with Flatiron and IQVIA.

Our countermeasures include $50 million in payer VBAs targeting 30% coverage; expanded $0 copays for NOV-GLP1 reducing abandonment 18%; $75 million AI-RWE platform yielding ICERs under €30,000/QALY; emerging markets to 25% revenue by 2026 with Brazil filing; and 15+ years exclusivity via ADCs and gene editing.

While expecting flat-to-down 2-4% net realization in FY24, we're set for mid-teens growth.

Next, our R&D expense and pipeline investment priorities underscore this. Q3 R&D was $452 million, or 28% of revenue, up 15% YoY but flat sequentially. Full-year at $1.8-1.85 billion, or 26-27% of revenue. Oncology takes 42% or $760 million YTD for three Phase 3 readouts; immunology 22%; rare diseases 18%; CNS/cardiometab 18%. Intensity matches peers like Amgen; burn per program down 10% via 35% partnering.

Priorities: Oncology lead Nova-ADC-301 for HER2-low breast with $180 million for Phase 3 at 85% enrolled; immunology Nova-BiSep-47 for RA; CRISPR Nova-CRISPR-LC IND Q4; $150 million APAC via WuXi. Pillars: AI precision via ProteoLens nominating 12 targets; modality mix 60% biologics/CGT; pruning reallocates $80 million. Growth 10-12% in 2025 for 5+ approvals.

Geographically, Q3 net sales $1.62 billion up 14% reported, 16% constant currency, led by ONCO-456 at $620 million and RHEUMAX-like IL-23. US 52% or $844 million up 11% on NSCLC/MSI labels but payer delays; Europe 28% or $454 million up 15% CC on tenders despite HTA rebates; RoW 20% or $324 million up 32% CC, emerging 42% of RoW or $136 million up 45%.

China $74 million up 62% on ONCO-456 12% PD-1 share, Shanghai plant at 85% utilization; LatAm $35 million up 38% on Brazil tenders; India/SE Asia $27 million up 32%. $250 million acceleration plan with 15 filings, local trials, $120 million capex for 70% localization, IQVIA registries.

Emerging now 8% total revenue, 25-30% CAGR to 2027 vs. 12-15% overall.

For revenue guidance and catalysts, raising FY24 to $6.5-6.8 billion, 22% growth midpoint, Q4 $1.7-1.75 billion, margins 82-84%. Oncology $4.0 billion 62%; cardiometab $1.0 billion up 150% on NOV-GLP1; rare/royalties $200 million. US $4.7 billion 73%; ex-US $1.8 billion up 18% CC.

FY25 initiate $8.0-8.5 billion, 25% growth. Catalysts: NOV-GLP1 CVD data Q1 2025 for $4 billion peak; ONCO-456 BLA H1 2025; China launches; ADC Phase 2 Q3 2025; CRISPR IND Q2; $1.2 billion CelluThera acquisition synergies.

On business development, Q3 deals: ex-China license ABX-301 bispecific to Kyowa Kirin $225 million upfront, $1.2 billion milestones, 18-22% royalties; $50 million CSL hemophilia EMEA; $30 million Takeda RSV APAC; $450 million Vireon CRISPR acquisition with $150 million CVRs; Merck IO expansion $100 million; Sinopharm JV $200 million obesity. Oncology 45% pipeline; 2-3 H2 deals.

Key assumptions: FY24 revenue on 35-40% US NOV-GLP1 share, stable ASP, China $800 million peak; pipeline 75% POS NVT-301, CRISPR IND; R&D 22%; OpEx 12%. Risks: 20-25% Phase 3 failure, biosimilars $300 million erosion, IRA 5-7% ASP, supply 8% COGS, geopolitics, patents. Mitigations: diversification, M&A $1-2 billion, ESG manufacturing.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Lisa Patel, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, Mike. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, we achieved three major regulatory approvals and two label expansions. For ONCO-456, FDA sNDA approval for first-line NSCLC with pembro, Phase 3 HR 0.58, PFS 14.2 months, ORR 68%; EMA PRIME, China NMPA. Companion diagnostic in 1,200 sites. RARE-ZEN label to ambulatory SMA Type 3, +5.2 HFMSE, doubles US patients to 4,500 at $2.4 million. IMMU-300 EMA for UC, 52% remission, US PDUFA Q4. RWE from 15,000-patient registry; $250 million regulatory science cuts review 28%. More sNDAs year-end. We expect topline readouts Q4 2024 and INDs H1 2025.

Next, Dr. Raj Singh will provide an update on our research pipeline.

Dr. Raj Singh, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. We are making significant strides in our early-stage research. Advancements include AI-driven targets de-risking 15 novel ones, cutting timelines 30%; PROTAC-ADC hybrids; mRNA/AAV for oncology vaccines; in vivo CRISPR for liver/ataxia; base editing from Beam. Portfolio pruning focuses high-NPV; partnerships externalize 35%. Oncology bispecifics, immunology T-cell engagers, rare CGT lead, with APAC acceleration. These position 28 assets for $2.4 billion peak near-term.

Now I'll turn the call over to Karen Lee, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Karen Lee, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Dr. Singh. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with strong uptake in NOV-GLP1 obesity/T2D segments and ONCO-456 NSCLC/melanoma. Marketing campaigns are proving effective in driving 25% WoW script growth via preferred formulary on CVS/Express Scripts 70% lives, patient access reducing abandonment 18%, digital tools for 500 bps margins. Emerging traction in China/LatAm/India via JVs, tenders, registries accelerating HTA 40%. Biosimilar offsets via bundles reaching 150,000 patients.

Finally, Tom Harris will discuss our manufacturing operations.

Tom Harris, Head of Manufacturing:
Thank you, Karen. Our manufacturing operations are running smoothly. Capacity at Singapore/Shanghai at 85%, dual-sourcing 80% APIs mitigates India/China risks for 99% uptime; $120 million capex localizes 70% emerging supply by 2026, cuts COGS 22%, ESG expansions Ireland/Singapore reduce carbon 20%. Key priorities: continuous manufacturing for 85% margins, CMC for CRISPR/ADC scale-up, resilience amid disruptions.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Dr. Rivera.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Tom. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Instructions for questions. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks. On pricing, with IRA risks and GTN at 48%, how are VBAs performing and any update on 2026 modeling?

Mike Chen, CFO:
Great question, John. VBAs on ONCO-456 hit 92% rebate avoidance with 15% lives covered, RWE strong. Modeled 25-30% haircut for small-mols post-2026, but biologics safe; $50 million payer co-dev targets 30% by year-end.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen, Morgan Stanley:
Dr. Rivera, on catalysts, what's the confidence in NOV-GLP1 CVD data and impact on peak sales?

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Emily, interim shows 22% MACE reduction in 15,000-patient trial; positive Q1 2025 could drive 20% share gain, $4 billion US peak like semaglutide trajectories.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee, JPMorgan:
For emerging markets, China growth impressive—any supply or regulatory hurdles ahead?

Karen Lee, Head of Commercial:
David, Shanghai at 85% utilization, Sinopharm JV de-risks NMPA; bridging for CAR-T mid-2025. GeoAccess subsidizes copays, 72% margins despite 65% pricing.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim, Barclays:
On BD, Vireon synergies and pipeline integration timeline?

Mike Chen, CFO:
Rachel, $20 million opex savings post-close; VRX-102 Phase I/II year-end, 4.2x NPV. Oncology to 45%, hedges immunology erosion; H2 more inbound.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes questions at this time.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaBiotech Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
